The one subdirectory the specs live in, under the caller's @root@ — this package's geometry constant.
A registry rooted at "monitors" therefore holds `monitors/specs/<name>` per spec and `monitors/next_id`
for the counter, and the counter sits BESIDE the subdirectory rather than in it, so listing the specs
never has to skip a row that is not one.

declarations.documentation:
@name@ back when it is ALREADY a legal store segment, or `null` when it is not — the gate every
model-supplied handle passes before it becomes a key. It is `store.safe_segment`'s charset judgement
with the canonicalisation REFUSED rather than applied: `safe_segment` would hand "Repo-1" back as
"repo-1", and deleting `repo-1` because someone typed `Repo-1` is deleting a DIFFERENT row than the
one that was named. So a name is accepted only if it is its own canonical form, which every name
`register` mints is.

The kind tag a minted name wears, canonicalised: @kind@ as `store.safe_segment` returns it, or
"fiber" when it is not a legal segment at all. A kind is the APP's own vocabulary (one word per arm of
its spec sum), so a kind that needs replacing is a caller bug — and this answers it with a name that is
merely less readable rather than with a key that means something else, because a fleet whose numbering
throws has no way to record the thing it was just told to run.

declarations.documentation:
REGISTER one @spec@ as desired and mint its durable name. The next number and the write happen in ONE
critical section of the shared place's serial domain (`store.shared_exclusive_as`), because minting is a
read-modify-write: two callers deciding at the same instant would otherwise mint the same name, and a
duplicate name makes every later handle ambiguous. The name is `<kind>-<n>` — kind first so a name reads
as its kind at a glance — and it is returned for the caller to fork under, so the store WANTS the fiber
before the fiber exists (the other order leaves a running fiber nothing remembers).

This is the only agent here that writes a spec. It does not fork anything, and nothing about the fiber
is its business — @spec@ crosses as `unknown` and is handed back to the caller's own validator later.
declarations.name: register

parameters.documentation: The registry root under the shared place, e.g. "monitors"; the PROGRAM's geometry, so a malformed path panics in `store.scope`.

declarations.documentation:
FORGET the spec named @name@ — the ONE door out of the desired set, and a DECISION: someone said this
should stop being wanted. Nothing here reacts to a fiber's DEATH, and that absence is the design. A
fiber that crashed, was cancelled or simply ended leaves its spec alone, so the next boot brings it
back; a fleet that pruned itself on death would shrink silently, and the store is the only record of
what was ever wanted.

TOTAL in both directions a caller cannot control: a name with no stored spec is a harmless no-op (so a
caller need not check first, and need not branch on whether a given fiber is one of this fleet's), and a
name that is not a legal store segment — a model's handle, a `gate:` or `mail:` fiber name — is ignored
rather than turned into a key. A single-key delete with no read-modify-write, so it takes no critical
section.
declarations.name: forget

listing a roster join and a handle lookup want: neither needs the spec parsed, and a row whose spec no
longer parses must still be VISIBLE to them (a listing that silently omitted it would report a standing
order as gone while it is still there, waiting to be re-forked at the next boot). Single-key reads over
a listing, so no critical section; reach for `sweep` when the unreadable ones should be dropped rather
than shown.

declarations.checkedType: agent(root: string, validate: agent(value: unknown) -> (null | T2)) -> sweep_result[T2] with throw[validation_error] | shared
declarations.documentation:
SWEEP the desired set: read every stored spec, hand it to @validate@, KEEP the ones that parse and
DELETE the ones that do not — answering with both halves. This is the boot move, and the reason it is a
sweep rather than a read is that a stored spec can go bad without anyone touching it: a cell edited by
hand, or a spec shape that changed across a deploy. Neither may fail a boot (the rest of the fleet has
standing orders too), and neither may sit in the store forever pretending to be a standing order.

@validate@ is the caller's own TOTAL parser (`json.try_validate[Spec]` is the whole of it in practice):
this package cannot know the spec type, so the type travels through the callback and back out in
@kept@ — which is what stops a caller from validating once here and to use the answer again. Its row is
fixed to NOTHING, so a validator that throws or reaches the network will not type-check here, and that
is deliberate: a sweep runs before the fleet is up and must not be able to stall there. T is read off
the callback's result and inference does not reach into an argument's return type, so instantiate it —
`fleet.sweep[my_spec](...)`.

DELETING IS NOT A DECISION ABOUT THE FIBER. What `sweep` drops is a row nobody can read, which is the
one case where leaving it costs more than losing it; a row that reads fine is never touched, however
dead its fiber. @dropped@ is returned rather than reported because the sentence belongs to the app —
this package does not know who should hear about it.
declarations.name: sweep

parameters.documentation: The registry root under the shared place.
parameters.label: root

parameters.documentation: The caller's TOTAL validator: the parsed spec, or `null` for a value that no longer conforms.
parameters.label: validate

declarations.signature: agent sweep[T extends unknown](root: string, validate: agent(value: unknown) -> T | null) -> sweep_result[T] with store.shared | prelude.throw[json.validation_error]

declarations.documentation:
PLAN the reconcile: the pure difference between the DESIRED names and the LIVE ones. @missing@ is
desired-and-not-live — what a boot forks, and what a listing shows as persisted-but-not-running.
@orphans@ is live-and-not-desired — what a reconciler would stop.

Nothing is read, written or acted on: this is the reconcile DECISION with the acting left out, in one
place, so a fleet's several callers cannot each derive the difference slightly differently. Order is
preserved from the input lists.

WHAT IT DOES NOT GUARANTEE: @orphans@ is only about this fleet if @live@ holds this fleet's fibers
ALONE. A nursery that also carries sources, crons, approval fibers or queued mail will list every one
of them as an orphan, because nothing desires them and nothing here can tell them apart. Pass a live
list you have already narrowed, or use @missing@ alone — which is well defined whatever else is
running, since a desired name is this fleet's by construction.
declarations.name: plan

parameters.label: desired
